newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPE must get SIMEX consent to list on NYMEX-source.
newsitem.headline: IPE must get SIMEX consent to list on NYMEX-source.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) of London would require the agreement of Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) to list its Brent crude futures contract on the New York Mercantile Exchange's out-of-hours electronic trading system, industry sources said on Thursday.
The provision was written into the Link Trading and Clearing Agreement signed by the IPE and SIMEX in 1995 to set up Brent trading on SIMEX, the sources familiar with the terms of the agreement said.
They said the accord called for the mutual agreement of the IPE and SIMEX if Brent was to be traded on an electronic or any other trading system operated by the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX).

A SIMEX spokesman said its Link Trading and Clearing Agreement with the IPE gave SIMEX the trading rights on the Brent contract between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. in Singapore (2200 GMT to 1000 GMT) or 5 a.m. and 5 p.m. in Singapore during London summer time.
NYMEX President Patrick Thompson told Reuters on Monday that NYMEX and the IPE were considering the launch of Brent trade on NYMEX's out-of-hours ACCESS system.
NYMEX ACCESS is open between the hours of 1600 EDT (2100 GMT) and 0800 EDT (1300 GMT), covering all SIMEX opening hours.
Thompson said Brent on ACCESS would be the first step for further development of the electronic system, currently used solely to trade NYMEX contracts outside of New York open-outcry trading hours.
NYMEX and the IPE have scheduled an announcement on the proposed link-up later on Thursday.
SIMEX declined comment on the NYMEX/IPE talks or their implications for SIMEX.
The IPE said it was in discussions with SIMEX on a a number of issues, including talks on how to restore confidence in Brent trade on SIMEX.
Singapore traders say Brent's listing on NYMEX Access would deal a major blow to Brent trade on SIMEX and raise questions over the IPE's five-year pact with the Singapore exchange.
Brent was launched on SIMEX in 1995 under a mutual offset agreement, where positions opened on SIMEX could be closed on the IPE and vica versa.
But the SIMEX market has been dogged with poor volume of just a few hundred lots per day, compared with 40,000 to 50,000 lots on IPE.
The IPE already has requested that SIMEX bring forward its Brent close by half an hour to allow the IPE to open trade at 0930 GMT instead of 1000 GMT.
